explain.say: Here is what can go in a calm corner. Soft things: a cushion, a blanket, a soft toy. Calm tools: ear defenders, a squeeze ball, a picture book, a breathing card. Brilliant! Your challenge: plan a calm corner at home.

faq.q: How do I know I need the calm corner?
faq.a: Check your body. A hot face, tight fists, a fluttery tummy or too much noise in your head are signs.
asks: Tell me about Notice my feeling

faq.q: What do I say to use the calm corner?
faq.a: You can say, Can I go to the calm corner, please? Some schools use a card you can show instead.
asks: Tell me about Ask to go

faq.q: How long do I stay in the calm corner?
faq.a: Usually a few minutes, until your body feels softer. A timer can help. Then you come back.

faq.q: Is the calm corner a punishment?
faq.a: No. It is a helper, like a plaster for feelings. Anyone can use it to calm down.

faq.q: What goes in a calm corner?
faq.a: Soft things, like a cushion and a blanket, and calm tools, like ear defenders, a squeeze ball and books.

facts: Many classrooms have a calm space where children can go to settle big feelings.
A calm corner works best when you use it before feelings get very big.

options.show: A cosy place to calm down
options.say: A cosy place to calm down

quiz.why: It is a helper space where you can settle your body and feelings.

wrong.1: It is not a punishment. Anyone can use it.
wrong.2: It is quiet and calm, not for loud games.

quiz.say: What can you say to use the calm corner?

options.show: Can I go to the calm corner, please?
options.say: Can I go to the calm corner, please?

quiz.why: Asking lets your teacher know where you are and helps you.

wrong.1: Asking politely helps more than shouting.
wrong.2: Running off can worry your teacher.
